products.name: Deepgram
products.note: Speech recognition API; real-time transcription; model customization; on-prem option

reading.body:
Deepgram consolidates speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and voice agent APIs into a single platform to reduce latency and complexity for enterprise customers, positioning unified voice AI as an alternative to assembling separate services.

Voice interfaces are computationally expensive at scale. Speech recognition and synthesis both require models running continuously, and Deepgram's on-premises option suggests customers want to avoid external API calls for latency-sensitive applications. The company's positioning around LLM orchestration and its recent Flux TTS model indicate that voice is increasingly treated as a frontend to language models rather than a standalone capability, meaning compute requirements compound when speech and text inference stack together.

The free build period with stated connection limits (45 concurrent streams in the US, 5 elsewhere) reveals infrastructure constraints that shape customer deployment options. The asymmetry between regions hints at where Deepgram's compute is provisioned. These limits do not reflect a technical floor but a commercial one, and they will bind tighter as voice AI adoption scales across enterprise applications.

This data does not cover Deepgram's actual compute footprint, power consumption, or whether its infrastructure is company-owned or cloud-rented. It shows what the company offers and how it frames customer problems, not the electrical cost of serving those customers at scale.
